title: TVClaude: Retro Terminal UI for Claude Code Now Available
summary: TVClaude brings Turbo Vision-style text UI to Claude Code, offering a nostalgic terminal interface for AI-powered development workflows.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- TVClaude launches as an open-source terminal UI wrapper that brings retro Turbo Vision aesthetics to Claude Code workflows.
- The project recreates the classic DOS-era text interface style, offering developers a keyboard-driven alternative to modern GUIs.
- Early community response on Hacker News shows interest in nostalgic developer tools that prioritize efficiency over visual polish.


A new open-source project has brought 1990s-era terminal aesthetics to modern AI development. TVClaude, released November 14, 2026, wraps Anthropic's Claude Code in a Turbo Vision-style text user interface, offering developers a keyboard-driven alternative to contemporary graphical tools. The project surfaced on Hacker News with early adopters praising its nostalgic approach to AI-assisted coding.


## What TVClaude Offers


TVClaude recreates the distinctive look and feel of Turbo Vision, the text-based UI framework that powered Borland development tools in the early 1990s. The interface features characteristic bordered windows, drop-down menus, and dialog boxes rendered entirely in ASCII characters. Developers interact with Claude Code through keyboard shortcuts and menu navigation rather than mouse clicks.


The project targets users who prefer terminal-based workflows or work in environments where graphical interfaces are impractical. By layering a retro UI over Claude Code's capabilities, TVClaude maintains full access to the AI assistant's code generation, review, and debugging features while presenting them through a decidedly old-school interface.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 14, 2026, TVClaude is available as an open-source project on GitHub. The tool requires an existing Claude Code subscription and runs in standard terminal emulators across Linux, macOS, and Windows. Installation follows conventional command-line package management workflows, with documentation covering setup for multiple operating systems.


## Technical Architecture


The project builds on modern terminal UI libraries to recreate Turbo Vision's visual language without requiring actual DOS emulation. Key technical features include:


- Full Unicode support despite the ASCII-art aesthetic
- Responsive layout that adapts to terminal window dimensions
- Keyboard shortcut customization for power users
- Integration with Claude Code's API for real-time AI responses


The codebase separates presentation logic from AI interaction, allowing developers to modify the interface without touching Claude Code integration points. This modular design has already attracted contributors interested in adding themes and layout variations.


## Community Response


Early Hacker News discussion highlighted developer nostalgia for efficient text-based tools. One commenter noted that the stripped-down interface reduces visual distractions compared to feature-heavy modern IDEs. Others questioned whether the retro aesthetic serves practical purposes or simply appeals to sentiment.


The project's minimalist approach contrasts sharply with the visual polish of tools like[Claude Code vs Cursor](https://emergent.sh/learn/claude-code-vs-cursor) , which emphasize rich graphical interfaces and inline code suggestions. TVClaude instead prioritizes keyboard efficiency and terminal compatibility, positioning itself as a specialized tool for specific workflows rather than a mass-market alternative.


## What This Means


TVClaude represents a broader trend of developers revisiting command-line interfaces as modern software grows increasingly complex. While graphical tools dominate AI-assisted development, terminal-based alternatives continue attracting users who value speed, scriptability, and minimal system resource usage. The project's success will depend on whether its retro interface delivers genuine productivity gains or remains a curiosity for enthusiasts. For teams already invested in terminal workflows, TVClaude offers a way to integrate Claude Code without abandoning familiar development environments.
